prose_updates.related_work: Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn (2026, AISTATS, Theorems~1--6) establish general sharp COT bounds, continuity, and statistical guarantees. Their Theorem~1 is the closest identification anchor: it supplies sharp identification under a compact covariate domain, compact convex ambient outcome domain, overlap, and a continuous objective. The affine binary endpoint and every collision claim here are separately proved, and alternating embedded signs need not satisfy their later uniform smoothness or rate hypotheses. Hirano and Porter (2003, Theorem~3) provide the closest standard LAN and local asymptotic efficiency ingredient; what is inherited is the limit-experiment template, not the present likelihood calculation or transfer. The deterministic-shell theorem newly proves the matching ordered bounded-truncated-quadratic local-minimax lower and upper bounds only for the binary uniform-cell shells. Its extension to a full anchor-containing class is converse-only by submodel monotonicity. Ji, Lei, and Spector (2023, Theorems~3.1--3.5) provide model-agnostic dual inference and emphasize binning loss, but do not optimize honest expected length or identify this collision frontier. Ober-Reynolds (2023) derives sharp OT intervals and root-\(n\) inference in an instrumental-variables noncompliance model, not sparse covariate collisions. Paninski (2008) and Kipnis (2026) show that collisions govern sparse large-alphabet testing; Kipnis's supported-mixture architecture is especially close, but concerns one-sample uniformity testing. Arratia, Goldstein, and Gordon (1989, Theorem~1) supply dependency-neighborhood Poisson approximation. Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005, Theorem~1 and Corollary~1) and Stoye (2009, Propositions~1--2) inform confidence-set duality and boundary repair, but do not supply the admissible tail truncation, likelihood modulus, endpoint expansion, or exact rational verification here. Low and Zhou (2007) and Armstrong and Koles\'ar (2021) motivate the restricted pushforward and bias-aware scope, without supporting an upper claim over a full smoothness ball.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The former two-fixed-array lower witness is invalid because armwise marginal imbalance reveals the endpoint without cross-arm collisions. Every lower bound therefore uses mixtures supported on legal arrays and pays the discrepancy between the mixture index and the realized \(L_K\). The displayed Poisson-tail Chernoff certificate is valid only on the declared domain \(m+1>\lambda_s^+\); no arbitrary-truncation certificate is claimed. Floating-point linear-program output may only propose a basis: a certificate exists only after every likelihood, tail, action-length, primal, and dual quantity is outward-rounded and the rational inequalities are checked exactly. Endpoint decisions may be clipped to \(\mathcal D\) without increasing absolute or squared loss, but projection of \(\widehat L_K\) onto the narrower \(\mathcal A\) is excluded from the local Gaussian theorem because it changes boundary risk. The broader local classes need not be nested in \(H\), so their transfer uses \(\liminf_{H\to\infty}\), not an asserted limit.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The finite-\(\lambda\) comparison and decision theorems concern the realized endpoint \(L_K\) over the full legal deterministic-array class. Rational interval certificates require computable inputs, the admissibility condition \(m+1>\lambda_s^+\), and exact outward-rounded likelihood, tail, action-length, primal, and dual checks; floating-point output alone is not a certificate. The sparse theorem gives unprojected studentized Gaussian inference, while the matching ordered local-minimax variance theorem is confined to interior deterministic shells in the binary uniform-cell submodel. Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn's Theorem~1 supplies the closest general identification anchor, and Hirano and Porter's Theorem~3 supplies a standard LAN template; neither supplies the shell theorem proved here. Embedded finite-array laws meet the anchor's compact-covariate, compact-convex-outcome, continuous-cost conditions, so global and local results transfer to every containing class only as converse lower bounds. There is no broader-class collision upper bound or equality. Continuous achievability transfers only through the declared interpolation-image kernels; no raw total-variation comparison is asserted between continuous covariates and discrete labels. No claim covers unknown amplitudes, nonuniform cells, nonnegligible triple collisions, or a full continuous smoothness class. Coarsening changes the endpoint unless a separate bias theorem is supplied.
